336611.title: The perfect Skolem set conjecture
336611.statement:
Let $A = \{a_1,a_2,\dots,a_n\}$ be a set of positive integers with $a_1 < a_2 < \dots < a_n$. A **Skolem set** is a set for which $\{1,\dots,2n\}$ can be partitioned into pairs whose differences are the elements of $A$. **The perfect Skolem set conjecture.** The set $A$ is a Skolem set if and only if the number of even $a_i$ is even and

$$
\sum^n_{i=m} a_i \leq n^2-(m-1)^2
$$

for each $1 \leq m \leq n$. This proposes that the elementary parity and density conditions are also sufficient for ordinary sets, although the corresponding existence problem for multisets is substantially harder.
336611.source_name: Gustav Nordh, “A note on X-rays of permutations and a problem of Brualdi and Fritscher”, arXiv:1707.03928 (2017).
336611.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2005–2017). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:math/0506155](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0506155).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1707.03928

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2017).

355158.title: Product formula for successive vertex orderings of the line graph of a bipartite 3-uniform hypergraph
355158.statement:
Let $K_{m,n}^{(1,2)}$ be the $3$-uniform hypergraph on $V=V_1\cup V_2$, with $|V_1|=m$ and $|V_2|=n$, whose edges satisfy $|e\cap V_1|=1$ and $|e\cap V_2|=2$. Let $L(K_{m,n}^{(1,2)})$ be its line graph, and let $a_i=(m-i)\binom{n-2i}{2}$. Define

$$
d_i=\frac{a_0-a_i}{i}.
$$

**Product-formula conjecture.** The number of successive vertex orderings satisfies

$$
\sigma'(L(K_{m,n}^{(1,2)}))=m\cdot\prod_{i=1}^{m-1}\frac{mn-\binom{m+1}{2}+\binom{i}{2}}{d_i},
$$

where each fraction is evaluated after disregarding all zero factors in both the numerator and denominator.

The paper presents this as a product formula complementing an earlier summation formula. Its status is not resolved in the supplied text.
355158.source_name: Lixing Fang, Hao Huang, Janos Pach, Gabor Tardos and Junchi Zuo, “Successive vertex orderings of fully regular graphs”, arXiv:2206.13592 (2022).
355158.references:
**6 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2005–2022). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1806.07180](https://arxiv.org/abs/1806.07180), [arXiv:1608.06053](https://arxiv.org/abs/1608.06053), [arXiv:1210.2220](https://arxiv.org/abs/1210.2220), [arXiv:1207.0074](https://arxiv.org/abs/1207.0074), [arXiv:math/0501005](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0501005).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2206.13592

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2022).

357168.title: The Kauffman–Harary conjecture for prime-determinant alternating knot diagrams
357168.statement:
Let $D$ be a reduced alternating diagram of a knot $K$ with determinant $p$, where $p$ is prime. A **Fox $p$-coloring** is a coloring of the arcs of $D$ by elements of $\mathbb Z_p$ satisfying the crossing relations, and it is non-trivial when not all arcs receive the same color. **Kauffman–Harary conjecture.** Every non-trivial $p$-coloring of $D$ assigns different colors to different arcs.

The conjecture was proved in full generality by Mattman and Solis using pseudo-colorings, so it is no longer open.
357168.source_name: Rhea Palak Bakshi, Huizheng Guo, Gabriel Montoya-Vega, Sujoy Mukherjee and Józef H. Przytycki, “The Generalized Kauffman-Harary Conjecture is True”, arXiv:2301.02645 (2023).
357168.references:
**3 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2005–2023). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:0906.1612](https://arxiv.org/abs/0906.1612), [arXiv:math/0512088](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0512088).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2301.02645

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of January 2023); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “solved”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

376825.title: Global maximality of the circular leaky loop
376825.statement: Let $H_{\alpha,\Gamma}$ be the planar Hamiltonian with attractive interaction of strength $\alpha>0$ supported by a loop $\Gamma$ of fixed length $L$, and let $\epsilon_1(\alpha,\Gamma)=\inf\sigma(H_{\alpha,\Gamma})$ be its principal eigenvalue. The paper proves that the circle locally sharply maximizes $\epsilon_1(\alpha,\Gamma)$ within the specified class of curves. **Global maximality conjecture.** The circle is a sharp global maximizer of $\epsilon_1(\alpha,\Gamma)$, even under weaker regularity assumptions. This extends the proved local result to a global isoperimetric statement for leaky loops; the supplied text does not establish the global claim.
376825.source_name: Pavel Exner, “An isoperimetric problem for leaky loops and related mean-chord inequalities”, arXiv:math-ph/0501066 (2005).
376825.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math-ph/0501066

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of January 2005).

378986.title: Analyticity of the giant-component fraction away from the critical point
378986.statement: Let $\rho(c)$ denote the giant-component fraction as a function of the scaling parameter $c$, and let $c_0$ be the critical value. Theorem~5(i) establishes analyticity under condition (t5a). **Analyticity conjecture.** Theorem~5(i) holds without condition (t5a): $\rho(c)$ is always analytic except at $c_0$. This is proposed as an extension of Theorem~5(i); the supplied text gives no resolution status.
378986.source_name: Bela Bollobas, Svante Janson and Oliver Riordan, “The phase transition in inhomogeneous random graphs”, arXiv:math/0504589 (2006).
378986.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0504589

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2005).

379035.title: The homotopy-test-graph conjecture for connected bipartite graphs
379035.statement: A graph is a **homotopy test graph** if its Hom-complexes detect graph colorability through the corresponding homotopy-connectivity bound. **Homotopy-test-graph conjecture.** Every connected bipartite graph is a homotopy test graph. The claim generalizes the known case of connected bipartite graphs equipped with a ${\mathbb Z}_2$-action that flips an edge; the source gives no resolution of the general statement.
379035.source_name: Dmitry N. Kozlov, “Chromatic numbers, morphism complexes, and Stiefel-Whitney characteristic classes”, arXiv:math/0505563 (2005).
379035.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0505563

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of May 2005).

379053.title: The perfect extremal Skolem set conjecture
379053.statement:
Let $A=\{a_1,a_2,\dots,a_n\}$ be a set with $a_1>a_2>\dots>a_n$ and total sum $\sum_{i=1}^n a_i=n^2$. A **perfect extremal Skolem set** is a perfect Skolem set satisfying this extremal equality. **The perfect extremal Skolem set conjecture.** The set $A$ is a perfect extremal Skolem set if and only if the number of even $a_i$'s is even and

$$
\sum^m_{i=1}a_i\leq m(2n-m)
$$

for each $1\leq m\leq n$. This is the extremal special case of the perfect Skolem set conjecture. The source notes that the analogous assertion fails for multisets, but gives no separate resolution for ordinary sets.
379053.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0506155

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of June 2005). “The conjecture does not hold when we allow the sets to be multisets.”

379055.title: The distinct displacement-pattern conjecture for permutations
379055.statement:
Let $S_n$ be the symmetric group, and let a **displacement pattern** be a tuple $\alpha=(a_1,a_2,\dots,a_n)$ recording the displacements of a permutation, with the entries distinct. The necessary conditions are

$$
\sum^m_{i=1}a_i\leq m(n-m)\quad(1\leq m\leq n),
$$

with equality for $m=n$, together with the stated parity condition: if $n$ is even, the number of even entries is even, while if $n$ is odd, the number of odd entries is even. **The distinct displacement-pattern conjecture.** These necessary conditions are sufficient for the existence of a permutation $\pi\in S_n$ with displacement pattern $\alpha_\pi=\alpha$. The conjecture is identified as a special case of the perfect Skolem set conjecture. The source gives no separate resolution status.
379055.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0506155

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of June 2005). “The conjecture does not hold when we allow the sets to be multisets.”

379199.title: The spectrum-polygon conjecture for standardized Laplacian matrices
379199.statement: Let $n$ be a positive integer, let a standardized Laplacian matrix of order $n$ be a matrix of the type considered in the paper, and let $S$ be the polygon defined earlier as the region containing the spectra of these matrices. **Spectrum-polygon conjecture.** The set of all eigenvalues of standardized Laplacian matrices of order $n$ coincides with $S$. The preceding theorem proves that every point of $S$ is an eigenvalue of some standardized Laplacian matrix of order $n$; the conjecture asserts the converse inclusion as well. The claim is presented as unproved in the source.
379199.source_name: Rafig Agaev and Pavel Chebotarev, “On the spectra of nonsymmetric Laplacian matrices”, arXiv:math/0508176 (2005).
379199.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0508176

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2005).

379317.title: Proper-subset conjecture for classical spatial graphs in virtual spatial graph theory
379317.statement: A **classical spatial graph** is a spatial graph represented by a classical graph diagram, and two such graphs are **virtually equivalent** or **classically equivalent** according to the virtual or classical graph-diagram moves, respectively. **Proper-subset conjecture.** If two classical spatial graphs are virtually equivalent, then they are classically equivalent. This conjecture asserts that classical spatial graph theory embeds as a proper subset of virtual spatial graph theory; the source identifies the question as important but does not provide evidence of a resolution.
379317.source_name: Thomas Fleming and Blake Mellor, “Virtual Spatial Graphs”, arXiv:math/0510158 (2006).
379317.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0510158

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2005).

379340.title: Ore's connected-graph product conjecture for edge invariants
379340.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph with $n$ vertices and no isolated vertices. Let $alpha(G)$ be its stability number, $sigma_e(G)=omega_e(\overline G)$ its edge-stable-set invariant, $omega(G)$ its clique number, and $omega_e(G)$ its edge-clique-covering number. **Ore's conjecture.** If

$$
alpha(G)=sigma_e(G)\qquad\text{and}\qquad omega(G)=omega_e(G),
$$

then

$$
omega_e(G)sigma_e(G)\leq n.
$$

The source presents this as an answer to an open question posed by Ore and as a variant for connected graphs of Turán's theorem; the supplied status is open.
379340.source_name: Isidoro Gitler and Carlos E. Valencia, “On bounds for some graph invariants”, arXiv:math/0510387 (2013).
379340.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0510387

Status: **open** according to the source (as of October 2005). “This is an answer to an open question posed by Ore in his book which is a variant for connected graphs of a celebrated theorem of Turan .”

379373.title: Neil White's symmetric-exchange conjecture for matroid toric ideals
379373.statement: Let $M$ be a matroid on the ground set $\{1,2,\ldots,n\}$. Fix a field $k$, let $S_M=k[y_B:B\text{ a base of }M]$, and let $I_M$ be the kernel of the homomorphism $S_M\to k[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ sending $y_B$ to $\prod_{i\in B}x_i$. Given bases $B$ and $D$, a **double swap** is a pair $b\in B$ and $d\in D$ such that $B\cup d-b$ and $D\cup b-d$ are bases. **Neil White's conjecture.** For any matroid $M$, the toric ideal $I_M$ is generated by the quadratic binomials $y_{B_1}y_{B_2}-y_{D_1}y_{D_2}$ such that the pair of bases $D_1,D_2$ can be obtained from the pair $B_1,B_2$ by a double swap. This conjecture is a proposed algebraic form of White's symmetric-exchange conjecture; the paper proves it for graphic matroids, while the general matroid case remains open.
379373.source_name: Jonah Blasiak, “The toric ideal of a graphic matroid is generated by quadrics”, arXiv:math/0511223 (2005).
379373.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0511223

Status: **open** according to the source (as of November 2005). “The following are both still open and together imply White's conjecture.”

379375.title: The matroid toric-ideal quadratic Gröbner-basis conjecture
379375.statement: Let $M$ be a matroid and let $I_M$ be its toric ideal, the kernel of the map sending each base variable $y_B$ to the corresponding squarefree monomial. **The matroid quadratic Gröbner-basis conjecture.** The toric ideal $I_M$ has a Gröbner basis consisting of quadratic binomials. This is presented as a variant of White's conjecture and would imply the normality Gröbner-basis conjecture for toric varieties $Y_M$ arising from matroids. The source states that it remains open.
379375.source_name: Jonah Blasiak, “The toric ideal of a graphic matroid is generated by quadrics”, arXiv:math/0511223 (2005).
379375.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0511223

Status: **open** according to the source (as of November 2005). “The following are both still open and together imply White's conjecture.”

379965.title: Strong Dantzig conjecture for fundamental deformations
379965.statement:
Let $D(d)$ be the graph of $d$-dimensional Dantzig figures under fundamental deformations, and let $E(d)$ be the subgraph with the same vertices whose edges correspond to good fundamental deformations.

**Strong Dantzig conjecture.** Every fundamental deformation of a $d$-dimensional Dantzig figure is good; equivalently,

$$
E(d)=D(d).
$$

The source explains that $D(d)$ is connected in the strong sense, so this conjecture would imply the Dantzig conjecture. It is presented as an open conjecture within the proposed approach to the Hirsch conjecture.
379965.source_name: Yuji Odaka, “An Approach to the Hirsch Conjecture”, arXiv:math/0608388 (2008).
379965.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0608388

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2006).

379987.title: The totally geodesic image conjecture for simplicial embeddings of pants graphs
379987.statement:
Let $\Sigma_{1}$ and $\Sigma_{2}$ be compact, orientable surfaces, and let $\mathcal{P}(\Sigma)$ denote the pants graph of a surface $\Sigma$. A subgraph is **totally geodesic** if every geodesic in the ambient pants graph joining two of its vertices lies entirely in the subgraph. **Totally geodesic image conjecture.** If

$$
\phi:\mathcal{P}(\Sigma_{1})\longrightarrow\mathcal{P}(\Sigma_{2})
$$

is a simplicial embedding, then $\phi(\mathcal{P}(\Sigma_{1}))$ is totally geodesic in $\mathcal{P}(\Sigma_{2})$. This is posed as a guiding conjecture concerning the geometry of pants graphs; the supplied text does not state any resolution, so the conjecture remains open.
379987.source_name: Javier Aramayona, Hugo Parlier and Kenneth J. Shackleton, “Totally geodesic subgraphs of the pants complex”, arXiv:math/0608752 (2006).
379987.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0608752

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2006).

379994.title: The conjecture on symmetric six-tuples solving Problem 1
379994.statement:
A six-tuple $(a,b,c,a,b,c)$ is called **symmetric** when its first three entries are repeated in the same order in the last three entries. Problem 1 asks which six-tuples have the required property described in the paper.

**Symmetric six-tuple conjecture.** All symmetric six-tuples $(a,b,c,a,b,c)$ are solutions of Problem 1.

This conjecture is stated after the proof of the relevant obstruction-theoretic cases; the supplied text gives no further resolution or context.
379994.source_name: Pavle V. M. Blagojevic and Aleksandra S. Dimitrijevic Blagojevic, “Using Equivariant Obstruction Theory in Combinatorial Geometry”, arXiv:math/0609053 (2007).
379994.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0609053

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2006).

380003.title: Rational generating function conjecture for the class of permutations corresponding to pin words
380003.statement: A **pin word** is a word encoding a permutation through the pin sequence construction; the set of permutations corresponding to pin words forms a permutation class. **Rational generating function conjecture.** The class of permutations corresponding to pin words has a rational generating function. This conjecture concerns the enumerative structure of the permutation class arising from pin words and reflects the regular-language origin of the class. The supplied text gives no evidence of resolution.
380003.source_name: Robert Brignall, Nik Ruskuc and Vince Vatter, “Simple permutations: decidability and unavoidable substructures”, arXiv:math/0609211 (2006).
380003.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0609211

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2006).

380116.title: Positivity conjecture for normalized characters in twisted Boolean cumulants
380116.statement: For positive integers $k_1,\ldots,k_l$, let $\Sigma_{k_1,\ldots,k_l}$ denote the normalized character and let $\hat{B}_i$ denote the twisted Boolean cumulants. **Positivity conjecture for twisted Boolean cumulants.** The normalized character can be expressed as a polynomial in the twisted Boolean cumulants $\hat{B}_i$ with coefficients that are non-negative integers. This conjecture extends the observed positivity of the displayed examples and asks whether the positivity phenomenon persists when the shifted parameter is $\zeta=0$. Its resolution is not specified in the source.
380116.source_name: Amarpreet Rattan and Piotr Sniady, “Upper bound on the characters of the symmetric groups for balanced Young diagrams and a generalized Frobenius formula”, arXiv:math/0610540 (2007).
380116.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0610540

Status: **open** according to the source (as of October 2006).

380120.title: Simplicial affine oriented matroid bounded-complex conjecture
380120.statement: Let $(E,\mathcal{L},g)$ be a simplicial affine oriented matroid, where $g$ is the distinguished element and $\mathcal{L}^{++}$ denotes its bounded complex. **Simplicial bounded-complex conjecture.** Then the bounded complex $\mathcal{L}^{++}$ is a ball. This is an open question attributed to *Oriented Matroids* and is posed here as a conjecture for simplicial affine oriented matroids. Unlike the uniform-contraction case proved earlier in the paper, no resolution is given here.
380120.source_name: Xun Dong, “The bounded complex of a uniform affine oriented matroid is a ball”, arXiv:math/0610575 (2006).
380120.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0610575

Status: **open** according to the source (as of October 2006). “Another open question in asks whether the bounded complex of a simplicial affine oriented matroid is a ball.”

382572.title: Orthogonality conjecture for the four split decompositions
382572.statement:
Under Assumption, let $D$ be the diameter and let ${\tilde V}^{\downarrow \downarrow}_{ij}$, ${\tilde V}^{\uparrow \uparrow}_{rs}$, ${\tilde V}^{\downarrow \uparrow}_{ij}$, and ${\tilde V}^{\uparrow \downarrow}_{rs}$ denote the four split-decomposition spaces. **Orthogonality conjecture.** For $0 \leq i,j\leq D$, the spaces

$$
{\tilde V}^{\downarrow \downarrow}_{ij}\quad\text{and}\quad {\tilde V}^{\uparrow \uparrow}_{rs}
$$

are orthogonal unless $i+r=D$ and $j+s=D$. Moreover,

$$
{\tilde V}^{\downarrow \uparrow}_{ij}\quad\text{and}\quad {\tilde V}^{\uparrow \downarrow}_{rs}
$$

are orthogonal unless $i+r=D$ and $j+s=D$. This would describe the orthogonality pattern among the split-decomposition spaces under the stated assumption; the source gives no resolution of the conjecture.
382572.source_name: Tatsuro Ito and Paul Terwilliger, “Distance-regular graphs and the q-tetrahedron algebra”, arXiv:math/0608694 (2006).
382572.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0608694

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2006).
